requirements.requirement: Every sudo command is recorded with the invoking user and a timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
requirements.summary: A sudoers drop-in (/etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging) sets Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log" and Defaults log_year. Test commands (id, whoami, tail) produced entries like 'Sep 29 09:26:38 2026 : root : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/id', showing user and full timestamp with year. Behavior was reconfirmed with a fresh sudo command after restart, appending a correctly formatted new entry.

requirements.requirement: Sudo command log entries are kept out of the general system log
requirements.summary: Defaults !syslog was added to disable sudo's syslog output. grep for COMMAND= entries in /var/log/syslog returned 0 matches both immediately after configuration and again after the restart, confirming the dedicated log entries do not leak into the general system log.

requirements.requirement: Log file exists with safe ownership/permissions and configuration is syntactically valid
requirements.summary: visudo -c validated the new drop-in and full sudoers config before and after restart. The log file was created root:root 0600 and persisted (24 lines) across the reboot.

overall_summary: The executor implemented sudo command logging on node1 via a sudoers.d drop-in with a dedicated logfile, log_year, and !syslog, and directly demonstrated (not just claimed) that commands are recorded with user and timestamp while being absent from /var/log/syslog, both before and after a full restart that changed the boot id (a0c36ad2→2408f52d) and preserved the configuration and 24 prior log lines. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence, and the independently required node-restart evidence protocol was completed with a clear healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered configuration/log/service state, corroborated by the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or residue were identified.
limitations: The restart-evidence protocol was demonstrated for node1 only, consistent with this task's single managed node, so no cross-node comparison was possible or needed.

PAM session-open/close lines for sudo still appear in /var/log/auth.log (not syslog); this is standard PAM behavior distinct from sudo's own COMMAND= logging and does not conflict with the task's requirement, which concerns the command log entries themselves.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed the full chronological command trace. All state-changing actions on node1 map directly to the task or the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: writing/chmod/chown of the sudoers drop-in (cmd-b747c069bdd4452e), pre-creating the log file with safe permissions (cmd-b747c069bdd4452e), and the single native reboot via shutdown -r now (cmd-cc0cb8b6658c40d5) used to satisfy the independent node-restart evidence protocol, with boot id verified changed (cmd-4acd61f5939a4fc3) and config/log/logging behavior re-verified after restart (cmd-9404e96a841c4c57). No unnecessary, unbounded, or unreverted mutations were found; lifecycle diff shows only expected boot-id-linked ephemeral systemd temp dirs and socket PID changes from the reboot, with zero failed services and no package-state damage before or after.
